packageRules.description: One PR per service, never grouped. A bad image upgrade should be isolated to the service it breaks, and the portability check should be able to attribute the failure.

Major bumps need explicit approval from the dependency dashboard. Radarr and Sonarr run forward-only SQLite schema migrations, so a major upgrade is not reliably undone by pinning back to the previous digest - the database has already moved.

Digest-only updates are LinuxServer base-OS security rebuilds published under an unchanged version tag. These are exactly what digest pinning would otherwise freeze out, so they must keep flowing. Not automerged: that is a separate decision, not an implied one.

CI tooling majors need the same approval as image majors. Every rule above is scoped to the compose images, which left `.github/workflows/portability.yml` governed by nothing: `actions/checkout` and the `ubuntu` runner are picked up by the github-actions manager regardless. That workflow is the merge gate itself, so a breaking bump to it must be a deliberate act rather than an automatic PR.
